state.decision_rationale: Deferred as an experiment. Benchmark deterministic fixed, boundary-snapped, and symbol-primary partitions before changing exact packet bytes or coupling source transport to analyzer churn.

provenance.source_label: Kimi K3 critique: chunk boundaries are symbol-blind
provenance.review_target: MKTCTX/3 Continuum packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Fixed 64-line windows split functions mid-body. Aligning chunk boundaries to symbol boundaries when a boundary lands within about eight lines would improve retrieval and citation quality at near-zero cost.
feedback.normalized_claim: Allow exact chunks to move modestly around the target size when reliable symbol boundaries can preserve coherent functions, classes, or sections.

current_behavior: Exact content is split deterministically every 64 recognized source lines, except for the final remainder.
Chunk ranges provide bounded line anchors, and concatenating chunks reconstructs the exact content string.
Global symbol outlines are available before content but are not consulted by splitExactChunks.
Files with unavailable or partial outlines still use the same fixed-line algorithm.
evidence: src/context.test.ts: exact chunks preserve bytes and provide bounded line anchors

proposal.summary: Benchmark a deterministic boundary-snapping policy that uses trustworthy symbol ranges while preserving exact bytes and bounded chunk sizes.
candidate_changes: Define a target size and maximum deviation window for snapping to symbol starts or ends.
Specify tie-breaking, nested-symbol, oversized-symbol, overlapping-range, and unavailable-outline behavior.
Keep byte reconstruction exact and make chosen chunk boundaries deterministic inputs to packet identity.
Compare model navigation and citation accuracy across fixed, symbol-snapped, and single-chunk strategies.
non_goals: Do not make exact-content inclusion depend on analyzer availability.
Do not create unbounded chunks for very large symbols.
Do not assume semantic-looking chunks improve model outcomes without measurement.

questions: Which boundary is preferable when a symbol start and end are both nearby?
How much size variance preserves streaming and retrieval characteristics?
Should Markdown headings and other structural ranges participate alongside code symbols?
risks: Analyzer changes can churn chunk boundaries and packet bytes even when source is unchanged.
Snapping may create tiny adjacent chunks or conceal important cross-symbol context.
More complex chunking can impair simple consumers and reproducibility.
evidence_needed: Chunk-size distributions and boundary churn across representative languages.
Retrieval and citation evaluations with tasks whose answers cross fixed boundaries.
Determinism tests across analyzer versions and unavailable-outline cases.
